!!_WHO_CAN_GRANT_THIS: !! ONLY THE OWNER. A technical review can establish that the reconstruction is internally consistent and that every gate passes; it cannot establish that the reconstruction matches what the owner knows the apartment to be. Those are different claims and only the second unblocks the layout decision. No agent may set this to accepted.
!!_WHAT_ACCEPTANCE_DOES_NOT_MEAN: !! NOT AS-BUILT. What is accepted is that the PLANNED geometry is a faithful reading of the developer's drawings. `provenance` stays `planned` and `field_verified` stays false afterwards, and the +30/-45 mm build tolerance in dimension_tolerance.json continues to apply. Nothing here has been measured on site.
!!_THE_HASHES_ARE_THE_SCOPE: !! Approval is recorded against these BYTES, not against 'the drawing'. If any artefact changes, the acceptance LAPSES. !! AND THAT IS ENFORCED, NOT PROMISED: tools/layout/check_baseline_acceptance.py recomputes all three hashes on every run, compare_variants.py prints a PROVISIONAL banner when they do not match, and --require-accepted refuses outright. This sentence was prose alone until 2026-09-17, when nothing in tools/ or scripts/ read this file at all.

ventilation_shaft_v1_footprint.notes: !! NOT ACCEPTED AND NOT ACCEPTABLE TODAY. V1's footprint is unestablished - the basic-plan reading does not reconcile and the vault flags it as NEEDING A CAREFUL RE-MEASUREMENT. !!⚠ STATE CHANGED 2026-09-19 from `pending` to `excluded_pending_measurement`, and the reason is a DEADLOCK the gate had: it required EVERY scope to read `accepted`, so a scope that could never be accepted made the whole baseline permanently un-acceptable. Splitting the shafts into three scopes to avoid holding the rest hostage achieved nothing while the record itself was hostage. This state is a deliberate terminal exclusion, is disclosed separately by excluded_scopes(), can never read as accepted, and is only legal while the v1_footprint open measurement stays OPEN.

consequence_while_pending: v0 may NOT be promoted into the sheet the layout decision is read off - tools/cad/PROVISIONAL_MODEL_POLICY.md. compare_variants.py still RUNS; its output is simply not decision-bearing yet.
what_acceptance_unblocks: The single-basis v0/v1 comparison. !! AND THAT COMPARISON IS NOT A SELECTION OF v1. Its purpose is to identify which of v1's partitions actually earn their demolition and rebuild cost, measured on one consistent basis for the first time - a different question from which layout is nicer.
!!_THE_REVIEW_SHEET_IS_PINNED_TOO: !! It DEFINES what each accepted scope means - above all that accepting the shaft scopes does NOT settle V1's footprint. Unpinned, its wording could change after acceptance and quietly widen what was agreed.

open_measurements.blocks: any comparison or layout decision that turns on V1's CLEARANCE. V1's POSITION is separately reviewable and its size is not.

!!_ACCEPTANCE_MUST_UNBLOCK_WHAT_IT_CLAIM: !! The comparison reads data/outputs/variants/v0-existing/spec.json, NOT the accepted DXF - and that spec is an early schematic carrying its own `_retired` warning: 18 walls against 25, no ventilation shafts, a rectangular loggia. Until it is rebuilt from the resolved geometry, accepting the DXF would unblock a sheet built from the superseded file. check_baseline_acceptance.py now refuses on exactly this.
!!_hashes_are_newline_normalised: !! Text artefacts are hashed with CRLF folded to LF. git on Windows rewrites line endings on checkout, so a raw byte hash would lapse the owner acceptance on a fresh clone for a reason unrelated to the drawing. Binary artefacts are hashed raw, where the bytes ARE the content.
